labeling_method.labeler: The repository author, acting as the single human rater for this take-home. This is a real limitation, disclosed rather than hidden: with one labeller there is no inter-rater agreement figure, and the gold set inherits whatever systematic tendencies that one rater has.
labeling_method.procedure: The 18 model outputs in general_qa.json were authored first, each to exhibit one specific known defect (or none). The first 15 were then scored against config/rubric.yaml one criterion at a time, in case order, using the 1/3/5 anchors as the reference points. overall_score is a holistic integer judgment made after the six criterion scores, not their arithmetic mean -- the mean would double-count criteria that are correlated by construction on this suite. All labelling was completed and committed BEFORE any judge model was run against the set, so the judge's output could not influence a label.
caveats: n=15. At this size the confidence interval on any agreement coefficient spans most of the interpretable range; the interval, not the point estimate, is the result.

The labeller also authored the outputs being labelled. That makes the intended defect salient in a way it would not be to a blind rater, so these labels are probably cleaner and more internally consistent than a realistic human gold set, which biases agreement measurement in an unknown direction.
No washout re-label was performed, so intra-rater reliability -- the ceiling on any judge-human agreement number -- is unknown. Populate overall_score_relabel to compute it; the code path is live.
The suite is synthetic and English-only. Nothing here says anything about judge reliability on real production traffic, other languages, or long-context inputs.
